:::{#exm-relative-efficiency-mean}
#### Relative efficiency of two estimators of a mean

In [the example on two estimators of a mean](estimation.qmd#exm-mse-sample-mean) the sample mean has $\mselr{\bar X} = \varpar / n$
and the single-observation estimator has $\mselr{\Rvar_1} = \varpar$.
The relative efficiency of the sample mean with respect to $\Rvar_1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mselr{\Rvar_1}}{\mselr{\bar X}}
&= \frac{\varpar}{\varpar / n}
&& \text{(substitute the two mean squared errors)}\\
&= \varpar \cdot \frac{n}{\varpar}
&& \text{(divide by a fraction: multiply by its reciprocal)}\\
&= n \cdot \frac{\varpar}{\varpar}
&& \text{(reorder the factors)}\\
&= n \cdot 1
&& \text{($a / a = 1$)}\\
&= n
&& \text{($b \cdot 1 = b$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

so with $n = 50$ students, as in [the student-height example](estimation.qmd#exm-estimator),
the sample mean is 50 times as efficient as $\Rvar_1$.
:::
